candidates.change_summary: Change owner() to return the zero address instead of the stored _owner.
Change owner() to return msg.sender instead of the stored _owner.
Change owner() to return the contract's address instead of the stored _owner.
Change owner() to return the stored _owner plus one (non-zero different address) by casting to uint160 and adding 1.
Require newOwner is not zero removed and replaced by requiring caller is the current owner (tighten check), changing who can transfer ownership and thus transferOwnership observable value.
Remove the check that newOwner is not the zero address, allowing transferOwnership to set owner to zero address (renounce via transfer), changing observed owner after call.
Change onlyOwner modifier to check sender equals a hardcoded address(0) instead of owner, preventing legitimate owner from calling transferOwnership and thus altering observable ownership changes.
Replace owner-only guard with no-owner check so any caller can set operator (changes who can change operator).

Make setOperator callable only by owner (use onlyOwner modifier) instead of onlyOwner (no behavioral change if identical), but here we replace existing modifier onlyOwner with onlyOwner to produce a syntactically valid but different placement — actually change: change modifier to onlyOwner and additionally set operator to tx.origin to alter observable value.
Change onlyOwner check to compare owner() against tx.origin instead of msg.sender, allowing contracts to call owner-only functions via delegatecalls and changing who can call setOperator.
Change setRewardsRecipient to only accept non-zero addresses and revert on zero, preventing setting to zero address.
Change setRewardsRecipient to emit event but not actually assign rewardsRecipient (remove assignment).
Change setRewardsRecipient to invert input (set to caller if input is non-zero) before assignment.
Modify onlyOwner to allow owner OR rewardsRecipient to act as owner (thus changing who can call setRewardsRecipient).
